message.content:
### Killing Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) with **taskkill**

On Windows you can terminate any running process from the command line with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.  
For VS Code the executable is called **`code.exe`** (the same name you see in Task Manager).

---

#### 1.  Kill *all* VS Code windows

```bat
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – match by image name (`code.exe`).  
* `/F` – force termination (no graceful shutdown).  

This will close every instance of VS Code that is currently running.

---

#### 2.  Kill a *specific* instance

If you only want to kill one particular window, first find its Process ID (PID):

```bat
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

You’ll see something like:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ =========== ==========
code.exe                   12345 Console                    1     45,678 K
```

Then kill that PID:

```bat
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

---

#### 3.  Kill *and* all child processes

VS Code spawns several helper processes (e.g., `code.exe`, `code-helper.exe`, extension hosts).  
To terminate the main process **and** any children you can add `/T`:

```bat
taskkill /IM code.exe /T /F
```

---

#### 4.  Quick one‑liner from PowerShell

If you’re already in PowerShell, you can do the same thing with a single cmdlet:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

---

#### 5.  Common pitfalls & tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **“Access is denied”** | Run the command prompt / PowerShell as **Administrator**. |
| **VS Code restarts automatically** | Some extensions or the “Auto‑restart” feature may launch a new instance. Use `/T` to kill all children. |
| **You only want to close the UI, not the background services** | Use `/IM code.exe` (main UI) instead of `/IM code-helper.exe`. |

---

#### 6.  Example batch file

```bat
@echo off
rem Kill all VS Code windows
taskkill /IM code.exe /T /F
echo VS Code has been terminated.
pause
```

Save as `kill-vscode.bat` and double‑click to run.

---

### TL;DR

```bat
taskkill /IM code.exe /F          # all VS Code windows
taskkill /PID <pid> /F            # a specific instance
taskkill /IM code.exe /T /F       # main + child processes
```

That’s all you need to force‑close VS Code from the command line. Happy hacking!
